newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO sees support from crude, demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO sees support from crude, demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday is expected to rise on crude gains and Chinese demand, traders said.

Traders said Chinese buying for January has been steady. Most buyers were importing based on floating prices, they said. A Chinese bid was heard at $8 per tonne for cargoes delivery to south China in January.

Traders said prices were likely to rise above Thursday's $118.50/$120 per tonne assessment with further support seen from a local trader. The trader, heard to be bringing Iranian cargoes to Singapore is expected to be interested in keeping prices supported, they said
In the swaps market, January fuel oil was bid/asked at $119.25/$120.25 against Thursday's quotes of $118.50/$119.00 a tonne.
They said South Korean export supplies in January were capped, expected to be around December volumes, as domestic demand rises and production fall at the expense of rising gas oil output.
